# Dyna's CLIProxyAPI vendor

Dyna vendors this source for the v2 engine. The upstream repository is `https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI`. This subtree started at tag `v8.0.48` and now sits at tag `v8.0.49`, commit `250d598175db61a4e99ac38b9164ed04745754e5`. The module path is `github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/v8`. The upstream MIT license and all upstream notices remain unchanged.

## Dyna changes

P0 adds this documentation and changes no upstream CLIProxyAPI file. It changes no proxy behavior. The folder has its own `go.mod`, so the v1 root module and `go test ./...` skip it.

The v1 gofmt check, `scripts/ci-gofmt.sh`, skips this folder. One upstream test file does not pass gofmt, and Dyna keeps upstream formatting unchanged. This is a change to Dyna's script, not to the vendored source.

Each later patch to this folder must be its own commit. Each patch must add an entry here that names its reason and the Dyna code it serves.

- The SDK builder accepts an already-bound listener. `engine/model` uses it to avoid a loopback port reservation race that could expose the client key.
- Upstream PR [#5434](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/5434), head `fa29f0716067730b6aedbf3e3602ad7be489f9b7`, adds normalized Claude OAuth quota reports for `engine/model`. The patch changes upstream v7 import paths to v8; drop it when a subtree update includes the upstream change. Patch size: 812 lines added and 15 removed, including tests. The upstream body-cap test passed in 0.02 seconds on hermeslab.

- Preserve `seven_day_oauth_apps` alongside nonempty `limits` when the normalized limits omit that window. `engine/model` uses it for the correct Claude weekly quota. This separate patch adds 38 lines and removes 3, including its regression test; drop it when upstream fixes mixed responses.
- Preserve `five_hour` when nonempty `limits` omit an unscoped session window. `engine/model` needs the session quota for routing and display. The patch adds 12 product lines and removes 2, plus 27 test lines. The 2026-10-31 upstream issue and PR search found no matching patch; #5434 supplies the original endpoint. Drop this patch when upstream fixes mixed responses.
- OAuth in-memory handoff and adoption status: 124 product lines added, 4 removed. Dyna enables it for Claude and Codex callbacks, and it exposes adopted credential IDs for the supported flows. Upstream PR #4800 handles a busy callback port, not secret-free handoff; issue #295 asks for manual callbacks, not this storage boundary.
- Durable credential writes: 18 product lines added, 1 removed. An opt-in store rejects publication after a failed save with a typed, secret-free error. If a provider already invalidated the old token, the owner must sign in again. Upstream PR #6295 makes file replacement atomic but does not reject an uncommitted refresh.
- Codex metadata merge SDK bridge: 5 product lines added. The SQLite adapter reuses upstream’s `MergeCodexCredentialsFromDisk` rather than replacing token partitions on a metadata-only write. Upstream PR #3843 addresses the same preservation for file-backed stores.
- Durable API-key registration: `cmd/dyna` registers a stored key without a keyless fallback. Upstream issue #6201 asks for separate credentials and configuration; the checked open PRs do not implement this registration boundary.
- Staged credential activation: 21 product lines added, 6 removed. Credentials stay disabled until Dyna binds an account. A restart enables only credentials with a bound account. The 2026-10-31 upstream search found no fitting staged activation patch; PR #6715 covers a Codex login route.
- Shared OAuth/key staging hook: 7 product lines added, 1 removed. Both creation paths use the same disabled staging boundary; the upstream search for staged OAuth activation remains the same as above.
- Non-Codex completion adoption: 18 product lines added, 5 removed. It verifies the disabled runtime grant before the completion notification. The 2026-10-31 upstream OAuth adoption search found PR #4734 for Codex recovery, not this private handoff. A build-tagged test bridge joins the real management status and Dyna RPC paths without entering production builds.
- OAuth completion notification: 11 product lines added. A private hook tells the engine when a saved OAuth session completes, so unpolled attempts cannot leave a routable orphan. The 2026-10-31 upstream searches found no fitting completion hook; PR #6715 adds a Codex login route rather than a store handoff.
- Private credential discovery and typed runtime status: 83 product lines added. The SDK exposes pathless credentials to the local adapter. `RequiresSignIn` is runtime-only, so an unverified credential stays unknown. Upstream issue #4585 confirms file-path listing gaps; #6201 remains open, and no checked upstream patch covers this adapter.

- Atomic OAuth grant replacement for existing credentials: 69 product lines added and 4 removed, plus regression tests. It uses the existing per-auth mutation gate and registration epoch to discard refreshes from an older grant, while preserving upstream partition merges. The existing request-info seam carries raw new-grant identity captured before upstream merges old metadata, so Dyna can reject a missing or different identity without skipping that merge. `engine/model` uses it for safe account reconnect. The upstream search on 2026-10-31 found issue #6288 on retry and #4945 on relogin metadata, but no matching atomic refresh-versus-login patch; upstream #4734 addresses targeted Codex recovery.

- Request-scoped credential eligibility: the engine sends encoded bound credential IDs over its private proxy socket; the handler removes the header and captures the set in context. Local selection, affinity and retries must stay within that set. The 2026-10-31 upstream search found issue [#6972](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/issues/6972) for external single-ID dispatch and PR [#5660](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/5660) for provider prefixes, but neither implements a request-local multi-credential allowlist.

- OpenCode Go session forwarding adapts upstream PR [#5833](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/5833), head `6adf6ea6008c8fdbc934139d743ab030d0af55d2`, for the OpenAI-compatible executor. It uses the canonical session identity on streaming and non-streaming requests, without leaking it to unrelated providers. Drop this patch when upstream includes it.

- Private fixed-upstream Kimi and z.ai search: the proxy authenticates with its request access manager and selects only active credentials in the request's encoded allowlist. It retains secrets in the proxy and returns bounded, sanitized refusal reasons. The 2026-10-31 upstream search found no matching search endpoint; issue #5236 is unrelated. Dyna uses the v1 provider protocols and disables redirects.

- Upstream PR [#6467](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/6467), head `212ebf61df925158f43f8d8401e6ebc3b83be0e0`, records Meta's `response.subscription_usage` as passive `X-Meta-*` quota signals for the `auth-files/quota` Meta reader that serves `engine/model`. The PR is open and conflicts with `v8.0.49`, so this adapts it. It keeps the recording: 134 product lines added, 1 removed, plus 223 test lines. It drops the PR's forwarding of the event, because upstream's `TestMetaExecutor_FiltersSubscriptionUsageGlobally` hides the event from every client and Dyna's Pi does not read it. It drops the PR's reload hunk, because upstream's file-snapshot merge in `updateInternal` already keeps the observation. It also accepts the typeless payloads upstream's filter treats as this event. Drop this patch when upstream records the event.

- Meta device sign-in adoption: 1 product line changed, plus a 42-line test. `engine/model` binds a Meta account only after it sees an adopted credential, as for Kimi and xAI, so the Meta flow reports through the existing Dyna completion path. Meta OAuth itself is upstream; the 2026-11-01 check of `v8.0.49` found no adoption path for it.

- xAI `api-call` refresh through the manager: 17 product lines added, 128 removed, plus 5 test lines added and 2 removed. `resolveXAIToken` refreshed outside the credential's refresh lock and saved the result itself, and xAI reportedly rotates refresh tokens, so a concurrent refresh could spend the grant. It now calls `ForceRefreshAuth` behind a singleflight. This protects the `xai` credentials `engine/model` binds; Dyna's own usage reader sends the stored token and never refreshes. The 2026-11-01 check of `v8.0.49` found the old path unchanged upstream.

- Normalized usage for every provider, starting with Codex: 359 product lines added, plus 307 test lines. `engine/model` keeps its one `auth-files/quota` call per credential, and the owner decided usage reporting belongs in the proxy. Non-Claude entries add `state`, `balances`, and window `name` and `seconds`; Claude's entries and status handling do not change. `auth_files_quota.go` gains only two embedded structs and two dispatch checks, and each reader lives in its own `dyna_usage_<provider>.go`. A reader sends the stored credential, never refreshes it, follows no redirect and forwards no upstream body. It fails to `unknown`, `unreachable` or `rate_limited`, never to 0 or to an expired sign-in. Upstream refused quota in core (#7018, #5034), so this stays local and the plugin system stays off. Codex reads `wham/usage` as `openai/codex` backend-client does and classifies windows by `limit_window_seconds`. `DynaCodexUserAgent` reuses the executor's client identity. Upstream PR #4488 offers a different `/v1/account/limits` route for three providers in 1362 lines, so taking it would not reduce this code. Drop this patch if upstream ships per-provider usage.

- Kimi usage reader: 166 product lines added, plus 122 test lines. It serves `engine/model` from `/coding/v1/usages` on the credential's domain, as `kimi-code` managed-usage.ts does. Official parsing shows false zeros (kimi-code #4133, #3817, #4473), so when legacy counters and a ratio pool cover one duration and reset, the more exhausted reading wins (CodexBar #4306). Monthly pools always show, and `boosterWallet` is a display-only balance. Upstream PR #4373 adds a background API-key probe for cooldowns in 2622 lines, which does not replace this reader.

- xAI usage reader: 84 product lines added, plus 71 test lines. It serves `engine/model` from the `grok-build` billing call, with the proxy's npm-tracked client version. It reads `creditUsagePercent`, then the deprecated `monthlyLimit` and `used`. A missing percent is 0% only beside a complete weekly or monthly period, as T3 Code decided, and otherwise unknown.

- z.ai usage reader: 60 product lines added, 3 removed, plus 77 test lines. It serves `engine/model` with the raw key on a fixed host, as z.ai's plugin and cc-switch do. It classifies limits by `unit`, reads `CREDIT_LIMIT`, skips `TIME_LIMIT`, omits impossible reset times and checks the envelope, because a pay-as-you-go key answers HTTP 200 with `success` false.

- DeepSeek balance reader: 36 product lines added, 4 removed, plus 38 test lines. It serves `engine/model` and the Home balance from the documented `/user/balance`, one balance per currency. DeepSeek has no limit windows, and `is_available` false is a low balance, not a bad key.

- OpenCode Go usage reader: 50 product lines added, 5 removed, plus 54 test lines. It serves `engine/model` from `/zen/go/v1/usage` with no workspace header. `rate-limited` counts as 100%, and a 403 means no Go subscription, so it reads as unknown and not as a bad key.

- Meta usage reader: 33 product lines added, plus 52 test lines. It serves `engine/model` from the signals the #6467 patch records, with no request, because Meta has no usage endpoint. An account stays unknown until it serves a request. A window past its reset is stale, so it drops out rather than reading 0.

- Removal of the passive Codex quota signals from `DynaCredentials`: 40 product lines and a test removed from the patch above. `engine/model` now reads every provider through `auth-files/quota`, so nothing reads them.

- Credential-owned models for OpenAI-compatible providers: 54 product lines added, 4 removed, plus 44 test lines. `engine/model` lets the owner add a provider while the proxy runs, so a credential's `dyna_models` and `dyna_display_name` attributes replace the configuration catalog, and `DynaCredentials` reports the registry's models as the one source for accounts and profiles. This removes the `dyna-catalog-only` configuration option. Upstream has no runtime catalog per credential: the `openai-compatibility` models come only from configuration at `v8.0.49`.

- Unknown usage for providers without a reader: 6 product lines added, 2 removed, plus 11 test lines. `engine/model` keeps one `auth-files/quota` call per account, so an owner-added provider answers `unknown` with no request. Readers stay keyed by the stable preset IDs `openai-compatible-zai`, `-deepseek` and `-opencode-go`.

- DeepSeek negative balances: 12 product lines added, 9 removed, plus 10 test lines. An overdrawn account reports `total_balance` `-0.01`, and the reader refused it as it does a negative usage percent, so `engine/model` saw no balance. Balances now read through `dynaNumber`.

- Reset-aware routing, adapted from upstream PR [#7020](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/7020), head `b7ab0c79a05d281ba4ccaa502fb3b02dae5c7c60`: 953 product lines added, 13 removed, plus 1240 test lines. `engine/model` sets `routing.strategy: soonest-reset`, because unused quota is lost at reset. Upstream's maintainer closed quota-aware routing as not planned (#5782, #5816), and #7020 is open and conflicts with `v8.0.49`, so expect to carry this. Drop the selector only if upstream ships one that takes every provider's windows from Dyna's readers.
  - From #7020: the selector on the route-aware path, in-memory readings bound to `RegistrationEpoch`, the merge that keeps a reading when a read fails, the positive-weight filter, weighted round robin for ties, and `GET /v8/management/routing/status`, whose order `engine/model` reads for the active account. Dropped: `PUT routing/reset-hints`, because the readers run in this process and publish directly. Changed: a reading holds every window rather than one reset, and it lives on the Manager, so a selector swap on hot reload keeps it. One review finding on #7020 stays open: replacing an account in place keeps `RegistrationEpoch`. Dyna's reconnect refuses a different identity, so this does not arise here.
  - Not taken: PR #7040, same strategy name, reads only passive Claude, Codex and Devin headers, sends unknown accounts first as probes, which the owner reversed, and changes `scheduler.go` throughout. PR #6382 and #7062 are Claude and Codex only and larger; #6562 ranks by most remaining; #4674 polls in the background. None reads Kimi, xAI, z.ai or model-scoped windows.
  - Ranking, in `soonestResetOrder`, which both `Pick` and the status use. Among long windows (a day or more) that apply to the model, the one with the least left sets the account's deadline. Running clocks come first, earliest deadline first; then unstarted long windows, which can wait; then accounts with no reading, round robin; then API keys and prepaid balances, which cost money; then spent accounts, soonest to recover first. A model-scoped window applies only to its model. Equal deadlines go to more absolute quota left, using plan size when the credential names one, then ID. Claude credentials name no plan, so there the percentage decides.
  - Gates on cold picks, constants at the top of `dyna_soonest_reset.go`: 3% or less on a long window; 10% or less on one resetting over a day away; 5-hour use at 90%. Accounts past a gate sort after everyone not spent, so a pick never fails on one, and failover ignores them. An account on course for 90% of its 5-hour window sorts after other running accounts but before unstarted ones. The owner's brief asked for plain gates at 90% and 3%; `dyna_soonest_reset_sim_test.go` found this does as well on waste and better on everything else, and the pace rule must not outrank an unstarted account, because a clock started early expires half used. v1's score still does slightly better on unmet demand. Run the test with `-v` for the table.
  - Hot path: `Pick` reads memory only. A cold pick that finds a reading missing, ten minutes old, or past a reset requests a background provider sweep. Every usage read goes through `sharedQuota`, so Home's reads feed routing and readers of the same credential share a five-minute cache. A reading older than six hours no longer ranks an account.

- Request-local quota refusals for Dyna-managed credentials: `cmd/dyna/proxy_store.go` marks credentials that have a usage reader, except z.ai, and drops saved availability verdicts on load and save while keeping provider observations (including Meta's usage signals). `dyna_quota_policy.go` skips booking quota-class 429s and explicit credit exhaustion, but asks for a background read of the refusing credential, sharing the existing per-provider 10-minute cap and backoff up to two hours. `dyna_soonest_reset.go` filters accounts whose applicable readings are under ten minutes old and at least 100% used, before priority, pin, or affinity. If every otherwise-available account is spent, the proxy returns 429 and the earliest known account recovery (each account waits for its last exhausted window). This replaces `dyna_quota_recovery.go`: there is no remembered quota block for a reader to clear. z.ai's pacing, auth quarantine, Cloudflare, unsupported-model and typed capacity behavior remain upstream. Custom keys without a usage reader retain in-memory upstream cooldowns; the Antigravity executor's short gate is unchanged because Dyna no longer uses that executor.
  - Refused credentials' readings are invalidated in routing and the shared usage cache. Pending credential IDs coalesce per provider and run as soon as the cap allows. A read invalidated in flight cannot republish its result; its replacement still shares the per-credential singleflight with management reads.
  - Upstream seams in `sdk/cliproxy/auth`: `conductor_cooldown.go:1011` calls `dynaRecordQuotaRefusal` before mutating failure availability; `conductor_selection.go:586-599,615-617` excludes `dynaSpent` candidates and returns `dynaQuotaSpentError` when none remain; `conductor_execution.go:704,927` and `conductor_stream.go:516,631` stop the current credential's model pool as soon as `dynaQuotaRefusal` matches, including stream bootstrap. `conductor_execution.go:124,181,188,237,245,326` tracks quota versus other failures and marks a quota-only result at the request boundary.
  - Upstream seams in `sdk/api/handlers`: `handlers_stream.go:528` skips the optional bootstrap replay on a terminal quota result. `handlers_errors.go:122,149` and `claude/code_handlers.go:568,618,637` keep the reset hint and send `X-Should-Retry: false` plus the quota message PiG classifies as nonretryable. These seams are for Dyna's private model route and readings; ordinary retries and the z.ai rounds are unchanged.

- Session account choice: 59 product lines added, plus 138 test lines. `engine/model` sends the owner's choice in `X-Dyna-Pinned-Auth`, which its route always replaces, so a box cannot set it. A chosen account outranks affinity and gates. This does not use upstream's `PinnedAuthMetadataKey`, which filters out every other candidate, so a 429 on the pin would fail the turn and the owner ruled that out. Instead the choice applies after availability filtering, so an account that is cooling, refused this request, removed, outside the room's allowlist or spent by its reading falls through to Automatic. The 2026-11-01 search found no soft pin upstream.

- Room account preference: `dyna_room_prefer.go` (about 60 lines) and one hook after the pin in `SoonestResetSelector.Pick` and in `SessionAffinitySelector.Pick`, plus the header read in `handlers.go`; `WithDynaEligibleAuth` now shares its ID decoding. `engine/model` sends the room's preferred credentials in `X-Dyna-Preferred-Auth`, which its route always replaces. After availability filtering, the preferred credentials that are not spent and past no soonest-reset gate become the only candidates, and affinity and the order run over them; when none is left, selection runs as before. A pin still wins. Unlike a pin, a preference keeps the gates, so the room spills before the account runs out. Upstream has no per-request preference; Dyna's eligibility header is already local.

- Restoring an alias that lost its virtual server: 23 product lines added, 1 removed, plus 40 test lines. `claudeMCPAliasResolver.resolve` gave up on a name whose server part it did not know, so the name reached Pi unrestored and Pi answered `Tool ... not found`. An audit of the live v2 transcripts on 2026-11-01 found nine such calls from Opus through `engine/model`: `mcp__human_write` with the server dropped, `mcp__mcp__device_juice__spirit_write` with `mcp__` doubled, and `mcp__dyna__dilemma_edit` with the server swapped for a real one. On 2026-11-08 the scan of failed tool calls found `maid_bash` and `gossip_codemode` from Opus, with `mcp__` dropped as well, so the prefix is optional. Each keeps the keyed tool ID with its semantic suffix, which one alias of a request has, so that component alone restores it and a shared suffix does not. Upstream closed issue #7107, the same class without the `mcp__` prefix, and #6848 as not planned, and `v8.0.51` still has the old path, so expect to carry this.

- Kimi Responses custom-tool bridge, ported from upstream [PR #6945](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/pull/6945), head `1312bd22941941235943cba41ec0f946cbc43159` (related issue [#6215](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/issues/6215)): the Kimi executor and its `helps/kimi_responses.go` helper, with their tests, applied as a filtered diff through the PR's three bridge commits. Kimi's Responses endpoint rejects every custom tool but `apply_patch`, and Pi sends `codemode` as a grammar custom tool, so the executor turns custom tools, history and `tool_choice` into function form upstream and returns `custom_tool_call` to the client, streaming included. It serves the `kimi-k3.1-pro` sessions `engine/model` routes to the Kimi account, and covers every Kimi model ID without a model list. It leaves out the PR's Kimi thinking replay and Codex model changes. `dyna_kimi_codemode_test.go` adds a Pi-shaped round trip. Drop this patch when upstream merges the PR.

- Insufficient-balance exhaustion: 24 product lines added, plus a 25-line test. A 402 whose message says "insufficient balance" (issue [#4853](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI/issues/4853), DeepSeek) cools the whole credential as quota-exhausted, with the upstream retry hint or one hour, under the error code `insufficient_balance`; the routing status publishes it as `reason`. The match is on the message, not the provider, so any provider that says "insufficient balance" is out of credit. `engine/model` reads the reason to show the owner why routing skips the account. The cooldown rules treat only 429 as quota, so the 402 is cooled as 429 while the client still gets the 402. The 2026-11-03 search found no upstream fix for #4853; #6891 covers only xAI.
- Durable session affinity: new `sdk/cliproxy/auth/session_cache_persist.go` (about 100 lines) plus a test file, and a few lines in `session_cache.go` (a dirty flag set in `replaceAliasGroupsLocked` and `removeAliasGroupLocked`, `statePath`, `flushMu`, and a flush in `Stop`), `selector.go` (`SessionAffinityConfig.StatePath`) and `service_config.go` (the path in `routingRuntimeState`, `<authDir>/session-affinity.state`, set only when `AuthDir` is set). The session cache saves its live bindings with their absolute expiry within one second of a change and loads the unexpired ones at start, so a restart keeps each session on its account. TTL, invalidation and failover are unchanged. The LCP matcher is not persisted. Upstream keeps these bindings in memory only; no upstream fix found.

- Upstream error code on a cooling failure: 10 product lines added, 1 import, plus a 22-line test. When every credential cools after an upstream overload, the next pick finds none and fails as `auth_unavailable` (503) with the last upstream error only inside the message text; `BuildErrorResponseBodyWithError` then set the generic `internal_server_error` code, so the client saw `auth_unavailable: no auth available` and no cause. A 5xx failure that wraps an upstream error now keeps that error's own `error.code` (such as `server_is_overloaded`) in the response body. The cooldown is unchanged. The 2026-11-03 search of upstream found no fix.

- Claude Fable 5.2 ahead of upstream (PRs #2328 and #2329, 2026-11-09). Anthropic refuses `claude-fable-5-2` from Claude Code older than 2.1.290, and upstream presents 2.1.280 (upstream issue #7386, open with no fix when this landed). Three changes serve the `fable` profile in `engine/profiles.go`:
  - `internal/registry/models/models.json` gains a `claude-fable-5-2` entry.
  - The baseline Claude Code profile moves as a whole to 2.1.321, measured from the real client: the User-Agent, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.128.0 and Node v26.12.1 in `helps/claude_device_profile.go`, and the version in the billing header and system signing. Test fixtures and version-derived hashes move with it.
  - `isClaudeFable51Model`, `isClaudeFable51OnlyModel` and `claudeModelHasPerTurnEffort` also match Fable 5.2. A capture of Claude Code 2.1.321 in print mode on 2026-11-09 showed the same betas, body keys and thinking shape for 5.1 and 5.2; its interactive mode was not measured.
  Drop all three when a subtree pull brings upstream's own Fable 5.2 support, and take upstream's values where they differ.

- Short selection cooldown wait: `sdk/cliproxy/auth/dyna_admission.go` holds Dyna requests through model cooldowns of up to five minutes, with jitter up to 10% (a 250 ms minimum jitter window, capped at 30 seconds). A single 5m30s deadline bounds selection and retry-round waits together, without timing out an active generation. The waits honor request cancellation. Non-Dyna callers retain the upstream policy.
- z.ai retry rounds: Dyna's proxy store applies three additional rounds only to z.ai API keys; the global retry count stays zero. The OpenAI-compatible executor uses 60s for z.ai 1302 and 20s for 1305 when the provider sends no valid `Retry-After`. A streaming request can retry a failed bootstrap but never after the first payload; subsequent errors travel on the original stream. The box and engine model routes leave 11 minutes of wire idle time for the cooldown and upstream response.

- Antigravity backport from upstream `f5c5681a8361c9da53e93c60b6507816eee7468b`: take only the Antigravity section of `models.json` (including Gemini 4 Neon XHigh and Gemini 4 output caps), the Claude 5.5 thinking regression tests from `b63322b9c35a`, and the Antigravity OAuth refresh transport and tests from `0861f9e1d14a`, keeping the current JSON library. The Hub sign-in and forced-tool executor fixes (`02e9e8520405`, `1d45a5f33290`) are already in the base. This serves the models `engine/model` routes for Dyna profiles. The rest of the proxy stays pinned: upstream main's repository-wide JSON rewrite would require porting Dyna's OAuth, quota, and routing patches separately.

- Antigravity Hub client versions from upstream `f72f8bfd6a1c`, `f2b003035dbe`, `093c7efa`, and `2d50f315`: use the 2.35.1 fallback and verified changelist mappings (`2.34.0` -> `1026637980`, `2.35.0` -> `1028447422`, `2.35.1` -> `1029194470`) for accounts Dyna routes. The endpoint uses these values for model availability; an unmapped online version falls back to a known version/changelist pair.

- Model catalog sync from upstream `38fe9295` (`a5e8f69e`, `c1842be2`, `5b857ecc`, `19a0a854`, `c1040cc0`, `5f7c0553`, `5fec95cf`):
  - `internal/registry/models/models.json`: bump `gpt-6.2-sol` `context_length` to `500000`, update `gpt-6.2-astra`/`gpt-6.2-sol` metadata, and add `gpt-6-chat-thinking` in `codex-plus`/`codex-pro`/`codex-team`; add `gpt-6-chat-thinking` and remove obsolete `gpt-6.1-terra` in `codex-free`; align `claude-fable-5-2` `created` and `description` in `claude`; add `muse-ember-1.0` in `meta`; add `gemini-4-carbon`, `gemini-4-hydrogen`, `gemini-4-neon`, `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` and set `gemini-4-argon` `max_completion_tokens` to `65536` across `gemini`/`vertex`/`aistudio` as upstream. Omit `copilot` (not enabled in Dyna) and keep `antigravity` as synced at `f5c5681a`.
  - `internal/registry/models/codex_client_models.json`: synced to upstream `38fe9295` (`a5e8f69e`, `5f7c0553`, `5fec95cf`). Serves `engine/model` catalog lookup and Codex client model responses.

- Antigravity's management OAuth uses the same in-memory callback and verified completion handoff as the other Dyna sign-ins. The Dyna staging hook prefixes its model IDs with `antigravity/`, so `engine/model` keeps those routes separate from direct subscriptions. The upstream account probe still determines which models from the embedded catalog a credential serves. Dyna rejects an access-only grant before saving so a reconnect cannot discard a working refresh token.
- Antigravity usage follows [Quotio's parser](https://github.com/nguyenphutrong/quotio/blob/474bc2afc26a0dd1bee49decda720f74a100a713/apps/cli/src/providers/antigravity.rs#L239-L255) for `quotaInfo` in Google's `fetchAvailableModels` response. Dyna's shared quota reader polls independently of entitlement changes, so the display can refresh more often than the three-hour catalog probe. The readings have a model and reset time, not an invented window length. No paid credit fallback is enabled.

- Auth refresh and quarantine fixes backported from upstream (`95f125ff`, `7b4c64b0`, `a96e640d`, `e5827065`, `7df56074`, `0bfb3d01`), preserving Dyna's `v8.0.49` JSON/regexp stack, staged-disabled activation, durable store writes, registration-epoch guards, and `engine/model`'s runtime-only `RequiresSignIn` contract:
  - `95f125ff`: skip automatic Codex refresh when no local renewal credential (`refresh_token` or SIWC) is present.
  - `7b4c64b0`: preserve disabled credential refresh backoff and failure counts across refresh outcomes.
  - `a96e640d`: keep sign-in-required Codex credentials quarantined across forced/manual refreshes when rejected refresh tokens did not rotate, require a valid active access token before restoring active routing status, and return the redacted credential entry view from v8 `/credentials/refresh`.
  - `e5827065`: prevent auto-refresh spin for disabled credentials holding unchanged rejected refresh tokens by deferring to access token expiry or unscheduling while keeping `StatusDisabled`.
  - `7df56074`: back off non-refreshing auths whose `nextRefreshCheckAt` is in the past instead of spinning with zero wait.
  - `0bfb3d01`: match Anthropic's `"refresh token expired"` grant description in `isTerminalRefreshGrantMessage` and normalize it to `refresh_token_expired` in `terminalRefreshErrorCode` (ported onto Dyna's `v8.0.49` classifier without upstream's `refresh_outcome_unknown` / journal stack), so expired Claude refresh tokens mark `RequiresSignIn` while generic `invalid_grant` responses continue exponential backoff.

- Cooldown, credit, `count_tokens`, and registry expiry fixes backported from upstream (`0130d6f3`, `d00267c3`, `1c537211`, `69ed202a`), preserving Dyna's `v8.0.49` JSON/regexp stack, generic 402 `insufficient_balance` cooling and reason projection, the then-current Dyna quota reconciliation, credential-owned API-key models (`dyna_models`), and Antigravity `antigravity/` model prefixing:
  - `0130d6f3`: keep Fable-only 429 rejections model-scoped when 7d is allowed and 5h headers are omitted, so a Fable weekly limit does not cool the credential or block sibling Opus/Sonnet requests.
  - `d00267c3`: exempt Anthropic HTTP 400 `"Your credit balance is too low"` responses from request-fault classification, applying a 30-minute `payment_required` cooldown, cooldown view reason mapping, and session-affinity rebinding while keeping Dyna's separate 402 `insufficient_balance` cooling intact.
  - `1c537211`: keep `count_tokens` HTTP 501 and typed unsupported-capability errors availability-neutral and expose `ErrorCode()` on plugin RPC and auth error types, preserving explicit model-not-found, auth, and quota cooldowns.
  - `69ed202a`: align client model projections with selector `availabilityBlock` semantics and track per-client bounded suspension deadlines in `ModelRegistry` so expired finite cooldowns automatically restore `/v1/models` listings while open-ended disabled/unauthorized gates remain unbounded.

- Codex HTTP Chat Completions translator fixes from upstream `7ec25aaaf65aeda54fe8875b10ecb9701c36aa49` and `6065b82d0374ac2908df92a7ed8070bb6c516f1b`: track text by output item ID and index and emit `response.output_item.done` text only when the item did not stream it. Match partial keys to a sole compatible open item. When a streamed delta could belong to several items, retain the delta and skip fallback for those candidates rather than guessing by completion order. If a delta has no matching keys and an anonymous item was announced, or an unkeyed delta arrives with no known open item, disable fallback for the rest of that response. Deltas with matching keys keep normal fallback behavior. A response with no known keyed item or prior text may supply one nonempty anonymous done snapshot; later final snapshots are not replayed without an identity for that first snapshot. Take only the Chat output-text fallback prerequisite from `ca459712c0a787cac90fd65406c5e42c7d8e540a`; reset tracking on `response.created` as in `e442c32d4f82f38541d003561943993b9b8e6d1f`. Normalize null, blank and non-string Chat `reasoning_effort` to Codex's existing `medium` default, join all non-stream summary text parts, and translate `response.failed` and `error` when they reach the translator. The HTTP executor still handles terminal errors before translation so status, retry and usage accounting stay intact. This base does not share the Codex request converter with standard Responses; no standard Responses, refusal, Meta synthesis or WebSocket changes were taken.

- Kimi streaming correctness from upstream `914399f69c7d20ff746abc809ddc56171f2d1172` (released in `v8.1.5`), ported onto gjson and Dyna's existing stream/usage helpers. Chat Completions buffers each SSE event (50 MiB limit on lines and accumulated data), fails on upstream error frames or EOF without `[DONE]` or a primary finish reason, and keeps observed usage on failure. A read cut or size limit on an accepted stream is a typed 502 truncation, so it neither replays the request nor cools a credential. A complete upstream error payload still keeps its real status, even if the transport cuts before the delimiter. Native Responses settles cancellation against the delivered terminal frame, including when Dyna's tool bridge emits the whole frame in one chunk, and still forwards structured errors through the Responses handler. Kimi's custom-tool bridge, native usage projection and Claude Messages delegation stay in place. No shared executor, translator, or new provider paths are carried.

- xAI buffered HTTP Responses terminal errors from `949b43b330f919fddeeb45e27b90cc9413736ef7`: assemble split SSE JSON with the existing Responses scanner and surface explicit upstream errors, including JSON failures returned with HTTP 200. Keep the selected error envelope's details and fill missing fields from `response.error`, the top level, then `body.error`. Preserve the provider's reason, HTTP status and Retry-After (or the existing free-tier window). A read cut in a plain-text error line is local truncation; an intact JSON error or newline-terminated text retains its provider status. Empty/unterminated accepted POSTs use Dyna's typed stream-truncation error, which stops replay without cooling the credential. Only actual patch activity warrants an apply_patch error when there is no terminal response.
- xAI streamed HTTP Responses from `27e298cff4a191bce48706da0adab64d0502e8b0`: reuse the same parser and truncation policy, keep observed usage on failures and cancellation, and normalize response.done for translated clients without changing native SSE. The Responses handler acknowledges completed, incomplete and done frames after flush for executors that opt into delivery tracking. Preserve reasoning replay and the tool bridge. No moego conversion, xAI WebSocket, Meta, OpenAI-compatible, Copilot or Google executor changes.
- Meta terminal handling from `32625f13de765ff38fc195ff7e5e0ff7e0c9b07c` (first in `v8.1.3`), Meta-only `db276e8b1bfe90625ac9ad0e55243baf083f1d2a` (`v8.1.4`), and Meta-only `27e298cff4a191bce48706da0adab64d0502e8b0` (`v8.1.5`). Recognize `response.done` in native SSE, translated streams, and buffered SSE/JSON, preserving incomplete and explicit failure semantics. Reject malformed success envelopes before tool translation; inspect retained buffered events after a short read so a complete terminal or earlier usage is not lost. A locally truncated accepted request is a typed 502, not a replay or credential cooldown. Keep observed usage on failure and pre-terminal client cancellation; a disconnect after the terminal chunk does not turn success into failure. Keep native event names, output reconstruction, apply_patch translation, and passive subscription-usage capture; no xAI, compatibility, Copilot, Google, plugin, or CLI changes. Latest upstream checkpoint inspected: `v8.1.7` (`47f18e4d82bd72f7d2b5ecf5ede93e4837a4625e`); subtree base unchanged.

- OpenAI-compatible text streaming from `27e298cff4a191bce48706da0adab64d0502e8b0` (first in `v8.1.5`): retain usage from complete upstream SSE frames, distinguish cancellation before and after the rendered terminal, and reconcile Responses success with the existing HTTP delivery acknowledgment. Read cuts and malformed frames on an accepted request are typed 502 truncations, not provider throttles, replays, or cooldowns; intact provider errors keep their existing status and policy. Preserve Chat finish/`[DONE]`, translator-confirmed EOF, apply_patch, and OpenCode Go session forwarding. No Images, other provider paths, or retry-policy changes.

- Claude-to-Responses tool choice and failure handling from `7075ec9eedad1fc5c3a77e84fc2cf7792df10070` (first in `v8.1.5`). Translate `none` and filter `allowed_tools` before reconstructing history without changing Dyna tool identities, namespaces or OAuth aliases. Emit one `response.failed` with partial output and observed usage for an intact accepted Anthropic SSE error; an interrupted apply_patch remains incomplete and does not emit input completion. Buffer complete frames for Responses only, retaining the existing buffered HTTP error contract. A missing source terminator or malformed frame is a typed 502, not replay or cooldown. Claude Messages, Chat, cache and other providers are unchanged.

## Pulls

- `v8.0.49` (2026-11-01): `git subtree pull` merged with no conflicts. Every patch above still applies, and none is obsolete: PR #5434 stays open and unmerged, PR #5833 was closed unmerged. The release changes plugin login, Gemini sanitizing and Codex commentary through Claude clients. The commentary option defaults to off, so `engine/model` sees no change in routing, management paths or credential handling. `TestResponsesInterruptStopsHTTPUpstream` and `TestCodexClientModelsApplyPatchRouting` are flaky on `v8.0.48` with Dyna's patches too, and `TestEnsureClientsWaitsForPreviousTargetClose` fails there on every run, so this pull did not cause them; CI does not run them.

## Update

Run this command from the Dyna repository root, replacing `<tag>` with the new upstream tag:

```sh
git subtree pull --prefix=next/third_party/cliproxyapi https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI <tag> --squash
```

Keep the subtree commits in the Dyna history. Do not rebase or squash them away. Resolve any conflicts with Dyna's patches, then build and test the v2 engine.

## Verify the tree

The vendored files must equal the upstream tag, except for `DYNA.md` and any patches listed above. Run this from the Dyna repository root to compare the trees:

```sh
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir "$d/upstream" "$d/vendored" && git archive 250d598175db61a4e99ac38b9164ed04745754e5 | tar -x -C "$d/upstream" && git archive HEAD:next/third_party/cliproxyapi | tar -x -C "$d/vendored" && diff -r -x DYNA.md "$d/upstream" "$d/vendored"; rm -rf "$d"
```

The subtree squash commit that `git subtree add` created names the upstream commit in its message. Its tree equals the upstream commit's tree.
